# Staged GRPO / TACO experiment

The staged run is unhealthy. Held-out TACO accuracy never rose above the step-0 baseline, because GRPO advantages were laid out across tokens incorrectly and the policy update was noise.

## Root cause

`compute_grpo_outcome_advantage` in `verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py` computed the right per-sample scalar (group mean/std of the outcome reward), then destroyed the sample axis. It reshaped the length-`batch` score vector into a single row, padded or truncated that row to `response_length`, and `expand`ed the same row onto every sample before multiplying by `response_mask`.

Every response therefore received the same token-wise advantage pattern: sample `i`'s scalar was written onto token position `i` of every sequence (and dropped entirely when `response_length` was shorter than the batch). It was not broadcast along that sample's own response tokens. The vectorized GRPO helper in the same file still does the correct `scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask`. The launch script uses `algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo`, which is registered to the broken function, and `trainer.use_v1=False`, so `ray_trainer.compute_advantage` calls it.

That matches the frozen run under `logs/wandb/offline-run-20260926_105216-l7my3znq`:

- Held-out `val-core/taco/acc/mean@1` was 0.076 at step 0, then 0.049 / 0.060 / 0.071 / 0.043 / 0.054 at steps 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250. Pass rate stayed near 0.20. Training did not improve the test set.
- `critic/score/mean` stayed sparse but nonzero (about 0.03–0.33), and `critic/advantages/min` / `max` stayed at real GRPO magnitudes (about ±0.5 to ±2.47). The scalar normalization ran.
- `critic/advantages/mean` and `actor/pg_loss` sat around 1e-4 to 1e-3, with `actor/pg_clipfrac` stuck at 0 and `actor/grad_norm` drifting down (0.44 at step 1 to ~0.18 by step 283). With `entropy_coeff=0` and `use_kl_loss=False`, the policy loss is only that scrambled advantage, so the update does not reinforce the samples that actually passed tests.
- Response length grew (mean ~174 at step 1 to ~370–500 later) with `response_length/clip_ratio` 0, so generations were not truncated away. Rollout-vs-actor prob correlation stayed ~0.999, so the log-prob path was consistent. The failure is the advantage layout, not a dead rollout or a clipped response budget.

Training reward alone does not show this: sparse binary TACO rewards still produce a small nonzero batch mean. Only the held-out curve, together with a near-zero policy loss despite large per-token advantage extremes, shows the update was not learning.

## Changes

- `verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py` — in `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage`, after the per-sample group normalization, broadcast with `scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask` instead of padding one shared row to `response_length` and expanding it across the batch.

No launch-script, data, or reward-function changes. The script still logs to `$LOG_DIR` / `$WANDB_DIR`.

## Expected effect

`val-core/taco/acc/mean@1` (and `val-aux/taco/score/mean@1`, `val-aux/taco/reward/mean@1`) should rise above the ~0.076 step-0 baseline across later evals (`TEST_FREQ=50`). `val-aux/taco/pass_rate/mean@1` should move up with accuracy. Training `critic/score/mean` should trend up, and `actor/pg_loss` should leave the ~0 floor once advantages are aligned with the rewarded samples.
